nodes.label: Express.js to NestJS Migration
nodes.rationale: The backend was converted from Express.js to NestJS to gain dependency injection, guard-based auth, interceptor-based uploads, exception filters, and DTO validation in place of ad-hoc middleware. Environment variables were deliberately left unchanged so deployment config did not have to move in lockstep.

nodes.label: NestJS Dependency Injection Pattern
nodes.rationale: Services are marked @Injectable() and injected via constructor rather than required at module scope, which makes them mockable in tests and lets NestJS own lifecycle.

nodes.label: Guards Replace Express Auth Middleware
nodes.rationale: Authentication middleware became guards applied with @UseGuards(), moving auth from a global chain to a declarative per-route/per-controller concern.

nodes.label: AI Services Module (AI Provider Service)
nodes.rationale: A single AI Provider Service abstracts both OpenAI and Anthropic so callers do not bind to one vendor.

nodes.label: Stub Modules Pending Implementation (Jobs, Matching, Applications)
nodes.rationale: Jobs, Matching, and Applications were stubbed rather than ported so the NestJS shell could ship first; the legacy JS services (job-scraper, job-matching, application-agent) still await TypeScript conversion.
